Upon success, a new login session is created in discussion_board_user_sessions for audit and authentication. This registration operation strictly matches discussion_board_users schema columns without assumption of extra fields. Response structure follows the pattern required for authentication operations for "user" actor in the DiscussionBoard service.

Security: Registration is a public endpoint and does not require prior authentication. If an email already exists (as required by the unique constraint on email), the API returns a duplicate error.

Actor Integration: This is the initial entry point for an end user. It works with the login and refresh endpoints to enable full authentication and session flows for users. No sensitive data such as password_hash is ever returned in results, only through issued tokens as authorized output.

Business rules: Registration requires valid email, password, and display_name; avatar_url is optional and must meet business-imposed mute/size/format checks. The operation leverages explicit column comments for email uniqueness and profile requirements with proper post-registration session handling by writing to discussion_board_user_sessions.

Related Operations: This is the first operation in the authentication workflow, preceding login and refresh. It integrates cleanly with account update and password management endpoints, if present.
operations.description:
Registers a new user account in the discussion_board_users table by storing email, password_hash (hashed by the service), display_name, and optional avatar_url, leveraging schema constraints for uniqueness, length, and optionality. Does not set is_locked or deleted_at, ensuring the account is active upon creation. Soft deletion and locks are deferred to update/delete operations, not present on registration.

Implements full business rules for user credentials: unique email, non-empty display_name, secure password captured as password_hash (never plain text), and avatar_url accepted as optional per schema definition. Account locking and soft deletion fields are exposed for future permission or moderation flows only, not triggered here.

On success, immediately issues a new session in discussion_board_user_sessions, capturing session audit attributes: ip, href, referrer, and timestamps for security review. This aligns to the schema's session relationship for usage reporting, recovery, and compliance.

API strongly references the schema's author, display_name, password_hash, is_locked, and avatar_url columns, and enforces validation strictly per backend logic specified for those columns. No extraneous fields are considered. Avatar_url's presence is optional, matching the schema's handling of nullable values and enforced size/type.

Security is implemented using JWT token response structures, compliant with core DiscussionBoard requirements and the business logic described in actor flows. This endpoint sets up the foundational credential for all authenticated workflows for regular members.

Relates to login (next step in JWT issuance) and refresh (for session continuation), all using the same authorization actor. This endpoint never returns raw password_hash, but only returns tokens and session meta per IDiscussionBoardUser.IAuthorized structure.

Edge cases, such as attempting to delete an already deleted article or trying to delete articles locked for moderation, are handled gracefully with context-specific error messages as per the error-handling rules in the requirements. IDiscussionBoardUser.description:
Discussion board user entity. Represents an end user identity for login, authorship, and account management. Maps directly to the discussion_board_users Prisma model. Password hash is NOT included in this response.

- id: Primary Key (UUID). System-unique identifier.
- email: User's unique email address (login, notification, and recovery).
- display_name: Profile display name (attribution for articles and comments).
- avatar_url: Optional profile image/avatar URI (nullable).
- is_locked: Account lock/suspended/ban state (for moderation/security).
- deleted_at: Soft delete timestamp (null if active); indicates deactivated or GDPR-compliant removal.
- created_at: Account creation timestamp.
- updated_at: Last modification timestamp.

Sensitive authentication data (password_hash) is NOT returned. This DTO is used for administrative and self-profile endpoints and follows privacy best practices.

IDiscussionBoardUser.ISummary.description:
Summary DTO for a discussion board user -- lightweight representation suitable for attribution, references, and list displays. Contains only essential, safe-to-expose identity fields for profile/author use, and intentionally omits sensitive or heavy relation data. Based on the discussion_board_users table in the Prisma schema.

Use this summary object as the author reference in articles, comments, abuse reports, or anywhere a minimal user context is required. Refer to the full IDiscussionBoardUser schema for complete details.

id.description: Unique identifier for the user (discussion_board_users.id).

display_name.description: Display name for the user; shown wherever attribution is needed (articles, comments, moderation logs).

oneOf.description: Optional URL of the user's avatar image; null if not set.

avatar_url.description: Optional URL of the user's avatar image; null if not set.

display_name.description: Display name visible to others, associated with user profile and article/comment authorship. Length between 1 and 100 characters. Business rule: must be unique across active users.

email.description: Email address for account login, notification, and password resets. Must be unique in the system. Changing requires email verification workflow.

password.description: New password, plaintext (will be hashed and stored server-side). Only use this field to request a password change. Value must follow password strength and complexity policies. Do NOT submit if updating other fields only.

oneOf.description: Optional profile image/avatar URL. If supplied, must be a valid URI (JPEG/PNG image), up to 80000 chars. Use null or omit for users without avatars.

avatar_url.description: Optional profile image/avatar URL. If supplied, must be a valid URI (JPEG/PNG image), up to 80000 chars. Use null or omit for users without avatars.

IDiscussionBoardUser.IUpdate.description:
DTO for updating the user profile (display name, email, password, avatar) in discussion_board_users. Only the authenticated user may change their own account details. Cannot be used to lock, unlock, or soft-delete – those operations are reserved for admin/business workflows. schema: discussion_board_users.

- Only supply password if changing, otherwise omit.
- Email must be unique, changing triggers verification.
- Avatar is optional, must be image URL if present, up to 80000 chars, URI format.
- Never include fields such as id, is_locked, deleted_at, created_at, updated_at, or any system fields. These are not mutable via this DTO.
- All fields are optional and allow partial updates. Supply only those to be updated.

IDiscussionBoardUserSession.IRequest.description:
DTO for searching, filtering, and paginating discussion_board_user_sessions records for a given user account. Used to retrieve login session history, restrict results to certain IPs/times, and support security audit workflows.

- Provide page/limit for pagination.
- Use from_date/to_date to filter by session date/time.
- Use ip_filter to restrict to sessions from specific client devices, offices, or remote IPs.
- sort_by/sort_order control ordering of results.
- active_only filters for sessions that are still valid/non-expired. All fields optional; default is most recent sessions first.

id.description: Unique identifier of the user session record within the system. Primary key, globally unique. Corresponds to the 'id' column in discussion_board_user_sessions.

discussion_board_user_id.description: References the owning user account (discussion_board_users.id). Only the session owner or authorized admin may access this session info.

ip.description: IP address from where the session was initiated. Used for audit and security review of sign-ins. Populated from client request or connection context.

href.description: The URL or page location at the start of the session. Useful for security and context in session-based analytics. Typically points to the page where login or authentication occurred.

referrer.description: The referrer URL present during session creation (previous page, external link, or empty for direct visits). Captured for session tracing or security analytics.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the session record was created. Used for session age tracking and timeouts. Read-only field.

expired_at.description: Timestamp when the session expired, or null if this session is still valid/active. Read-only field.

IDiscussionBoardUserSession.description: Represents a detailed login session record for a registered user in the discussion board system. Returned by authentication/session APIs, this object contains the key metadata for the session, including IP address, context (href/referrer), creation and expiration timestamp. Designed for account self-audit, device/session management, and admin review. This type is mapped to the discussion_board_user_sessions table in the database. Follows privacy, security, and compliance principles—only the owning user or admin may view full details. All properties are read-only.

page.description: Page number for paginated administrator account search results. Defaults to 1 if not provided.

limit.description: Maximum number of administrator summaries to return per page in search/list view. Defaults to 20, maximum 100.

display_name.description: Partial or exact match filter for administrator display name.

is_locked.description: Filter for admin lock/ban status. If true, only return locked admins; if false, only unlocked ones; if omitted, no filtering.

deleted_at.description: Filter: only include administrator records with this 'deleted_at' state (soft-deleted if set, active if null). Optional.

created_at_end.description: Filter: Include only admins created on or before this timestamp.

IDiscussionBoardAdmin.IRequest.description: Request schema for advanced querying, filtering, and paginating the list of administrator accounts in the discussion board platform. Enables search by text, filtering by lock/delete state, date ranges, and sorting. All query fields are optional—unspecified filters yield unfiltered results. Designed for admin management and compliance review interfaces, matching fields in the discussion_board_admins table. No business logic fields appear here—strictly for API-level queries or filters as described in administrative endpoint docs.

id.description: Primary key. Unique identifier (UUID) for the administrator account in the discussion_board_admins table, used for authentication, audit, and all moderator actions.

email.description: Administrator's unique email used for privileged login, escalation notices, audit traceability, and notifications. Must be unique in the system.

display_name.description: The display name for the administrator, shown in moderator tools, platform audit logs, and team identification. May be the real name or handle as configured by administrator.

oneOf.description: Optional avatar/profile image URL for the admin. May be null if not set. Used for identification in UIs and logs.

avatar_url.description: Optional avatar/profile image URL for the admin. Nullable.

is_locked.description: Indicates if the administrator account is currently locked, suspended, or banned for security or compliance reasons. True if access is disabled.

oneOf.description: Timestamp of soft deletion (if present, admin is deleted/banned). Field may be null for current accounts.

deleted_at.description: Soft delete timestamp for GDPR or key rotation purposes. Null if the account is not deleted.

created_at.description: Timestamp of administrator account creation for audit and traceability.

updated_at.description: Last time the administrator profile was modified.

IDiscussionBoardAdmin.description: Administrator account profile representing privileged actors empowered to moderate and control the discussion board system. Includes all fields from discussion_board_admins with compliance and audit attributes. Used for admin profile display, audit trail, and role/lock review. Fulfills requirements for full admin identity, account verification, and privilege introspection. Returned by admin detail query endpoints. Refer to the discussion_board_admins Prisma schema for the authoritative field list.

email.description: Administrator's new unique email. Must remain unique; used for login and notification. Changing this field updates the primary contact email for the account.

display_name.description: The updated display name for the administrator, used for transparency in logs and moderation tools.

password_hash.description: Updated hashed password for authentication. Never accepts plaintext; must be a strong hash. Enrollment or change triggers compliance audit log.

oneOf.description: Updated avatar or profile image URL for the admin.

avatar_url.description: Optional updated avatar/profile image URL for the admin. Nullable.

is_locked.description: If true, locks or suspends the administrator's account for security or compliance purposes.

oneOf.description: (Optional) Timestamp for soft deletion or GDPR/account rotation. Null if the account remains active.

deleted_at.description: Optional timestamp of soft deletion. If provided, marks the account as soft-deleted for compliance.

IDiscussionBoardAdmin.IUpdate.description: Update DTO for administrator profile and credentials, covering display name, email (must be unique), password hash, optional avatar URL, lock state, and optional deletion (GDPR/rotation). Used in admin profile update endpoints. Follows business rules for unique and validated fields. All fields originating from discussion_board_admins Prisma schema. Credential updates trigger audit/compliance logging.

page.description: Page number to retrieve for paginated session results. Used for paginating large session lists for administrators with many logins. Optional, defaults to first page if omitted.

limit.description: Maximum number of session records to retrieve per page. Used to restrict session history page size for audit and compliance. Optional, system may enforce max global limit (e.g. 50 or 100).

IDiscussionBoardAdminSession.IRequest.description: Request DTO for searching, filtering, and paginating administrator session records. Allows retrieval of relevant session records for compliance, audit, and self-service review. Supports status, IP, search text, and ordering/pagination fields. Based on discussion_board_admin_sessions requirements.

id.description: UUID-based primary key for the admin session record. Unique identifier for session trace, audit, and device management. Referenced in all session detail requests.

discussion_board_admin_id.description: Foreign key reference to the administrator actor that owns this session. Correlates with discussion_board_admins.id. Used to enforce session partitioning and audit trace.

ip.description: Logged IP address of the session's origin, per admin login. Used for incident tracing and security reviews.

href.description: Reported connection URL/location at session creation (often the login page). Useful for audit, diagnostic, or suspicious session pattern review.

referrer.description: Referrer location or web address responsible for the session's initiation, for audit compliance and unusual access investigation.

created_at.description: Session creation timestamp in ISO 8601 string format (UTC). Used for session lifecycle analytics, multi-device concurrency checks, and compliance history.

expired_at.description: ISO 8601 expiration timestamp (UTC) for this session, or null if still valid. Business logic uses null to indicate currently active session. Included for session history, security, and session management workflows.

IDiscussionBoardAdminSession.description: Detailed administrator session record as stored in discussion_board_admin_sessions. Returns all non-sensitive session context fields for audit and admin self-service. Credentials or sensitive authentication material are never included. Session status is identified by presence/absence of expired_at.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.IRequest.description: DTO for advanced search, filtering, and pagination of discussion board articles. Allows users to specify search criteria such as keywords (for title/body), author id, creation/update date ranges, sorting, and pagination options. Used in PATCH /discussionBoard/user/articles and similar article list endpoints. Only non-deleted articles are matched; result optimized for list views. All fields optional; at least one must be specified for effect.

q.description: Full-text keyword to search in article title and body. Applied with 'ILIKE' or trgm similarity for flexible fuzzy matching. Example: "inflation policy"

author_user_id.description: Filter to articles by a specific author's user ID. Must match an existing discussion_board_users.id. Example: "15f87f42-79aa-40ca-a6bf-01d6cfae69f1"

created_from.description: (Optional) Earliest article creation timestamp, inclusive. RFC3339 date-time string. Used for filtering results to articles created after/beginning with this instant.

created_to.description: (Optional) Latest article creation timestamp, inclusive. RFC3339 date-time string. Used for filtering results to articles created before/ending with this instant.

updated_from.description: (Optional) Earliest article last update timestamp, inclusive. RFC3339 date-time string. Used for filtering results to articles updated after/beginning here.

updated_to.description: (Optional) Latest article last update timestamp, inclusive. RFC3339 date-time string. Used for filtering results to articles updated before/ending here.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.description: The main discussion board article response DTO. Represents a single article with all detail fields, author summary, and associated non-deleted attachments. Used in GET /discussionBoard/user/articles/{articleId}, POST /discussionBoard/user/articles, and similar detail-and-create endpoints. Properties reflect the Prisma model plus FK transformations for API response: author is a summary object, attachments are detail array objects, and soft-deleted state is included. Comments are not directly embedded (accessed via separate endpoint).

id.description: Unique identifier for the article. Maps to discussion_board_articles.id.

title.description: Article title (1–100 characters, per business rule).

body.description: Main article body/content (1–10,000 characters, per business rule).

author.description: Summary of the article's author (FK transformation of author_user_id). Includes display name, avatar, and user id.

attachments.description: Array of non-deleted attachments (files/images) associated with this article. Each attachment includes metadata and storage info.

created_at.description: Timestamp when this article was created.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when this article was last modified.

oneOf.description: Soft delete timestamp. Null means not deleted; if present, article is hidden from standard user list.

deleted_at.description: Soft delete timestamp. Null means not deleted; if present, article is hidden from standard user list.

comments_count.description: Count of non-deleted comments on this article. Used for summary and navigation.

IDiscussionBoardArticleAttachment.description: Attachment entity for a file or image uploaded to a discussion board article. Corresponds to the 'discussion_board_article_attachments' model in Prisma. Returned in API responses for newly created or updated attachments. Contains all public-facing fields, including file metadata, virus scan status, logical kind, and soft deletion status. Sensitive internal references are omitted. All properties are read-only for clients.

id.description: Primary key (UUID) of the attachment record.

discussion_board_article_id.description: UUID of the parent article this attachment belongs to.

filename.description: Original uploaded file name as it appears in the record.

kind.description: Logical kind of the attachment: 'image', 'document', or 'archive'. Used by business logic for categorization and frontend display.

mimetype.description: MIME type of the file, e.g., 'image/png', 'application/pdf'.

virus_scanned.description: Whether this attachment passed virus/malware scan at upload time. True if safe, false or null otherwise.

created_at.description: Datetime when the attachment was uploaded and created in the system (ISO-8601 UTC, e.g., '2025-03-10T12:00:00Z').

oneOf.description: If present, ISO8601 datetime string when the attachment was deleted/removed from the article.

deleted_at.description: Nullable. Populated if and only if the attachment is logically (soft) deleted; otherwise, should be omitted or null.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.ICreate.description: Payload for creating a new discussion board article, supporting text content and optional file/image attachments. This schema enforces all business constraints, including title (1–100 characters), body (1–10,000 characters), and per-article attachment rules. The field 'attachments' accepts an array of IDiscussionBoardArticleAttachment.ICreate objects if optional files/images are uploaded. The authenticated user's identity is always derived from the session context and must not be supplied in the request (author_user_id is forbidden).

title.description: The title of the article. Required. Minimum 1 and maximum 100 characters per business rule.

body.description: Main article text body. Required. Minimum 1 and maximum 10,000 characters per business rule.

attachments.description: Optional image or file attachments for this article. Zero or more files/images can be uploaded as part of the article payload, up to the per-article and per-file type/size business limits. Each array element must conform to the IDiscussionBoardArticleAttachment.ICreate type.

IDiscussionBoardArticleAttachment.ICreat.description: DTO for creating a new article attachment (file or image) to associate with a specific discussion board article. This DTO corresponds to business requirements and the 'discussion_board_article_attachments' Prisma model; it enforces all business rules for allowed file types, file size, and security constraints. Intended for usage only by authenticated actors (author or admin) and never by unauthenticated clients. The parent article context ('articleId') is always provided in the API path/parameters and MUST NOT be part of this DTO body per security and atomic operation principles. Virus/malware scan results are populated by the backend after upload, so the client must not provide them.

filename.description: Original uploaded filename, including extension. Must adhere to business validation for allowed file types (JPEG, PNG, GIF, PDF, DOCX, XLSX, TXT, ZIP) and be a valid (non-empty) file name.

kind.description: Logical kind/category of attachment for business-level filtering. Expected values: 'image', 'document', 'archive'. 'image' for JPEG, PNG, GIF; 'document' for PDF, DOCX, XLSX, TXT; 'archive' for ZIP. Business logic at the backend verifies consistency with the file extension and MIME type.

mimetype.description: MIME type of the uploaded file, such as 'image/jpeg', 'application/pdf', etc. Must correspond with the file type and adhere to allowed formats in business rules.

filesize.description: Size in bytes of the uploaded file. Must not exceed maximum allowed file size as specified by business requirements (typically ≤10MB per file, but always validated server-side).

IDiscussionBoardArticle.IUpdate.description: Update payload for a discussion board article. Used for modifying the title, body, and current attachments of an existing article. Must comply with business constraints for allowable field changes and validation. For business and security reasons, the author's identity and articleId cannot be changed via this DTO (they are taken from context or path). All fields are optional; only provided fields will be updated. For modifying attachments, supply an array using IDiscussionBoardArticleAttachment.IUpdate objects if changing, otherwise omit.

title.description: (Optional) New title for the article, subject to minimum 1 and maximum 100 characters.

attachments.description: (Optional) Full replacement list of attachments for the article. Each array element must be an IDiscussionBoardArticleAttachment.IUpdate instance. Use to add, remove, or update attachments according to business logic. If this property is omitted, attachments remain unchanged.

IDiscussionBoardArticleAttachment.IUpdat.description:
DTO for updating an existing attachment (file or image) associated with a discussion board article. Fields follow PATCH semantics: all properties are optional, and updates will only be applied to provided fields. This DTO exactly maps to the 'discussion_board_article_attachments' Prisma model; however, only non-system fields can be changed (filename, kind, mimetype, filesize). Virus/malware scan results and deleted_at are managed only by the backend—never accepted here. Changing attachment 'kind' or 'filename' is permitted as long as business rules for allowed file types/extensions (JPEG, PNG, GIF, PDF, DOCX, XLSX, TXT, ZIP) and size limits (≤10MB/file) are obeyed. Use only for non-deleted attachments—soft-deleted attachments cannot be updated. Intended for author/admin updating their own article's attachments. Article and attachment IDs are in the API path, not this body.

- filename: (string, optional) If renaming/replacing the file, provide the new filename including extension. Must match allowed file types; required when updating the file itself.
- kind: (string, optional) Logical kind/category of attachment: must be one of 'image', 'document', or 'archive'. Should match file type if updating/replacing file. Example: 'image' for JPEG/PNG/GIF; 'document' for PDF/DOCX/XLSX/TXT; 'archive' for ZIP.
- mimetype: (string, optional) MIME type if file is being replaced or updated, e.g. 'image/jpeg', 'application/pdf'. Must match file extension and be an allowed type per business rules.
- filesize: (integer, optional) Size in bytes for the new or updated file, if replacing. Must respect business rule constraint (max 10 MB per file, backend enforced).

All fields optional—provide only those to be updated. Use in PATCH/PUT flows only; creation and deletion handled by other APIs. Security: Only author of the parent article or an administrator may update attachments.

filename.description: (Optional) Updated filename for attachment, including extension. Required if uploading new file; otherwise, may be sent to change label/filename. Must match supported types by extension: jpeg, jpg, png, gif, pdf, docx, xlsx, txt, zip. Business logic validates extension and name. No null allowed—omit if not updating.

kind.description: (Optional) Logical kind/category of attachment; must be one of: 'image', 'document', 'archive'. Should align with file extension. e.g. 'image' for JPEG/PNG/GIF, 'document' for PDF/DOCX/XLSX/TXT, 'archive' for ZIP. Use to correct categorization on file replacement. Omit or leave unchanged for existing file if not updating type.

mimetype.description: (Optional) MIME type for the attachment if updating or replacing file (e.g. 'image/jpeg', 'application/pdf'). Should match filename and kind. Only allowed MIME types per business/validation rules. Omit if not replacing file.

filesize.description: (Optional) Size of the updated file in bytes. Required if changing file itself or replacing attachment; must be ≤10,485,760 (10 MB). Omit if not updating file.

IDiscussionBoardArticleAttachment.IReque.description:
Filters and sorters for listing/searching attachments under a specific article. All fields are optional. Use for advanced query with the /attachments index endpoint. Only non-deleted attachments (deleted_at null) are returned. Each filter corresponds to a column in discussion_board_article_attachments and is validated per business logic.

- kind: (string, optional) Filter for logical kind/category of attachment; must be one of 'image', 'document', or 'archive'.
- filename: (string, optional) Case-insensitive partial or trigram match on filename, excluding extension if preferred—used for search. Example: 'plan' matches files named 'plan.pdf'.
- filesizeMin: (integer, optional) Minimum file size in bytes; filters out smaller files.
- filesizeMax: (integer, optional) Maximum file size in bytes; filters out larger files (max allowed = 10 MB).
- createdFrom: (string, optional, date-time) Only include attachments created at this timestamp or later (inclusive).
- createdTo: (string, optional, date-time) Only include attachments created at this timestamp or earlier (inclusive).
- page: (integer, optional) Result page to retrieve; defaults to 1 if omitted.
- pageSize: (integer, optional) Number of records per page; defaults to system default/max=100.
- sortBy: (enum, optional) Field to sort results by—one of 'created_at', 'filename', 'filesize'. Defaults to 'created_at'.
- sortOrder: (enum, optional) Sort order—'asc' (ascending) or 'desc' (descending). Defaults to 'desc' (newest first).

All properties are optional and may be combined for advanced search and paging. No property may be null; omit properties not used in the filter.

kind.description: Logical kind/category of attachment; valid values are 'image', 'document', 'archive'. Results filter to only those matching value. Use 'image' to restrict to JPEG, PNG, GIF; 'document' for PDF, DOCX, XLSX, TXT; 'archive' for ZIP files. Omit or leave undefined for 'all kinds'.

filename.description: Substring/trigram search on filename (case-insensitive). Find files whose names match substrings. Example: 'draft' matches 'draft1.pdf' and 'Q2-draft.xlsx'. Omit or leave undefined to include all files.

filesizeMin.description: If present, minimum file size (in bytes) to include in results. (e.g., 1024 = 1 KB+). Omit or leave undefined to include all sizes.

filesizeMax.description: If present, maximum file size (in bytes) for included results. (e.g., 10485760 = 10MB). Omit for no upper bound except for business rule enforced total limit.

createdFrom.description: ISO8601 datetime (inclusive lower bound) for filtering by attachment creation date. Returns only attachments created at or after this timestamp.

createdTo.description: ISO8601 datetime (inclusive upper bound) for filtering by attachment creation date. Returns only attachments created at or before this timestamp.

page.description: Page number for pagination. Results are divided into pages; starts at 1 by default if not set.

pageSize.description: Maximum results per page. Use to control pagination and result count. System will enforce any maximum (e.g. max=100).

oneOf.description: Sort by attachment creation time (default).
Sort by filename, alphabetically.
Sort by file size (bytes).

sortBy.description: Field by which to sort results. Supported: 'created_at', 'filename', 'filesize'. Defaults to 'created_at'.

oneOf.description: Results sorted in ascending order.
Results sorted in descending order (default; newest/largest/first).

id.description: Primary key for this comment entity. This field uniquely identifies each comment in the discussion_board_article_comments table.

discussion_board_article_id.description: ID of the parent article this comment belongs to. References discussion_board_articles.id. Enforces relational integrity and is used for context and lookup.

author.description: Summary information about the author of the comment. Derived from the author_user_id reference. See IDiscussionBoardUser.ISummary for details.

body.description: The text content of the comment. Required, must be between 1 and 1000 characters as enforced by business validation. Maps to the body field in discussion_board_article_comments.

created_at.description: The timestamp when this comment was created. For audit, chronological ordering, and display. Reads directly from created_at field.

updated_at.description: The timestamp of the most recent update to the comment. For edit audit trail and modified indicators. From updated_at field.

deleted_at.description: Soft delete marker for moderation/suppression. If set, comment is hidden from regular users but available for admin audit. Null means comment is visible. Maps to deleted_at field.

IDiscussionBoardArticleComment.description: Main entity representing a single comment under a discussion board article. Maps to discussion_board_article_comments table and provides context for UI rendering, audit, and moderation workflows. Includes author reference, timestamps, parent linkage, and soft-deletion handling suitable for all business, security, and compliance requirements.

page.description: Page number to retrieve. Required for paginated responses and must be >=1.

limit.description: Number of comment records per page. Required for consistent pagination. Valid range: 1–100, capped at 100 for performance.

author_user_id.description: Optional filter to restrict returned comments to those written by this user. Matches author_user_id FK.

search.description: Optional full-text search substring filter for comment body content. Uses trigram/partial matching and supports case-insensitive queries.

oneOf.description: Sort order for results. Either 'created_at-desc' (newest first, default) or 'created_at-asc' (oldest first). Must match one of the provided enum values. Default is 'created_at-desc'.
Sort order for results. Either 'created_at-desc' (newest first, default) or 'created_at-asc' (oldest first). Must match one of the provided enum values. Default is 'created_at-desc'.

sort.description: Sort order for results. Either 'created_at-desc' (newest first, default) or 'created_at-asc' (oldest first). Must match one of the provided enum values. Default is 'created_at-desc'.

include_deleted.description: If true, also include soft-deleted comments (moderator/admin context only). Ordinary users always receive false or null.

IDiscussionBoardArticleComment.IRequest.description: DTO used to request paginated and filtered comment summaries for article discussion threads. Supports pagination, author filtering, full-text search, results ordering, and (admin) deleted comment inclusion controls as needed for business flows.

body.description:
The textual content of the comment to be posted. Required, length 1–1000 characters. Must comply with business validation for comment posting. From discussion_board_article_comments.body.

Cannot be empty. Violations will be rejected with clear user-facing error. No images or attachments are supported in comments. Prohibited content is rejected as per business rules.

IDiscussionBoardArticleComment.ICreate.description: Request body for creating a new comment on a specific article in the discussion board. Creates a discussion_board_article_comments record. Linked to parent article by articleId in path; author is set from authentication context, never sent in request. Returns validation error if limits are violated or if the referenced article does not exist.

body.description:
The new textual content to update an existing comment. Length must be 1–1000 characters, per business rules. Updates the body field of discussion_board_article_comments.

If omitted, no change occurs. May only be changed by the comment's author or an admin. Violations or edits to deleted comments are rejected.

IDiscussionBoardArticleComment.IUpdate.description: Request body for updating (editing) an existing comment below a specific article. Allows changing the comment's content; field is optional but subject to validation. Linked comment and article IDs are provided in URL path; editing actor determined by authentication context (never sent in request body). Business logic rejects edits to deleted or non-existent comments. All successful edits update the updated_at timestamp.

IDiscussionBoardAbuseReport.IRequest.description:
Query parameter schema for filtering, searching, and sorting abuse reports (discussion_board_abuse_reports). Used by moderators/admins to search, filter, and paginate abuse reports for compliance or triage workflows. Excludes sensitive fields, only allows query-related criteria. No direct user identity permitted in public usage; used only by admins/moderators.

- Supports filtering by `abuse_category`, `status`, reporter user, article or comment id, creation/update date ranges, and full-text search by `reason`.
- Supports sorting and pagination.
- Related to the main discussion_board_abuse_reports schema for queries.

limit.description: Maximum number of results per page. Should respect system/page size limits (e.g., 10~100).

oneOf.description: Field to sort by. Allowed: created_at, updated_at, abuse_category, status.
Field to sort by. Allowed: created_at, updated_at, abuse_category, status.
Field to sort by. Allowed: created_at, updated_at, abuse_category, status.
Field to sort by. Allowed: created_at, updated_at, abuse_category, status.

sort_by.description: Field to sort by. Allowed: created_at, updated_at, abuse_category, status.

oneOf.description: Sort order for result. 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending.
Sort order for result. 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending.

sort_order.description: Sort order for result. 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending.

abuse_category.description: Filter for abuse type/category (such as 'spam','harassment','illegal', etc.). Must match allowed abuse_category values.

status.description: Filter for report moderation workflow status ('pending','in_review','closed','rejected', etc.).

target_article_id.description: Filter for reports targeting a specific article id.

target_comment_id.description: Filter for reports targeting a specific comment id.

reporter_user_id.description: Filter for reports submitted by a particular user (admin/internal only).

created_from.description: Filter for reports created on or after this ISO date-time.

created_to.description: Filter for reports created on or before this ISO date-time.

reason_search.description: Full-text search query on the 'reason' field.

IDiscussionBoardAbuseReport.description:
Full abuse report record as stored in the system, representing a user-submitted report of inappropriate, abusive, or policy-violating content (table: discussion_board_abuse_reports). Returned to moderators/admins from detailed review endpoints.

- Linked to user identities (reporter), target article or comment (mutually exclusive or both nullable).
- Includes business workflow/audit fields: current status, category, reason/explanation, creation/update metadata.
- System-generated fields present (id, timestamps). All fields reflect underlying database—no omitted audit data.
- Subject to business logic: only admins/moderators may view full detail; regular users only see their own created reports if endpoint permits.

id.description: Unique identifier of the abuse report (UUID, primary key).

reporter_user_id.description: User id (UUID) of the registered user who submitted this abuse report. Foreign key to discussion_board_users.

target_article_id.description: Article ID (UUID) targeted by this report (nullable if only a comment is targeted).

target_comment_id.description: Comment ID (UUID) targeted by this report (nullable if only an article is targeted).

abuse_category.description: Type/category of the reported abuse (e.g., 'spam','harassment','illegal'). Used in moderation workflow. See business/type enum.

reason.description: Free-text rationale for the report, as written by the reporter. Subject to validation and full-text search.

status.description: Current status of the abuse report in moderation workflow (e.g., 'pending','in_review','closed','rejected').

created_at.description: Timestamp representing when the abuse report was created (in ISO8601 date-time).

updated_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent status change or update to this report (in ISO8601 date-time).

IDiscussionBoardAbuseReport.ICreate.description:
Defines the request body for creating a new abuse report within the discussion board moderation system. This schema represents a user-submitted report against either an article or a comment, referencing the relevant target by UUID. Only authenticated users may create reports. The payload must include the abuse category and a detailed text reason/explanation for the report. One of target_article_id or target_comment_id is required.

All fields correspond directly to the properties of the discussion_board_abuse_reports Prisma model except for the reporter identity, which is obtained from the authentication context and must not be supplied in the request body. The initial status of all new reports is automatically set by the server (typically 'pending').

target_article_id.description: ID of the article being reported (optional if reporting a comment). Must reference an existing article. If null, report targets a comment.

target_comment_id.description: ID of the comment being reported (optional if reporting an article). Must reference an existing comment. If null, report targets an article.

abuse_category.description: Category of alleged abuse. Expected values include 'spam', 'offensive', 'harassment', 'illegal', etc. Enforced and whitelisted at the business logic layer.

reason.description: Detailed explanation for why the content is being reported. This text is recorded for auditing, moderation, and compliance, and is subject to length/business logic validation.

IDiscussionBoardAbuseReport.IUpdate.description:
Describes fields that can be updated on an existing abuse report. This schema is used by administrators only to change properties such as status, abuse category, or the report justification text. At least one field must be included. Only admins may perform this update operation.

All fields correspond to the discussion_board_abuse_reports database model. The report to be updated is uniquely identified in the API path, so no ID field is included here. The updated_at timestamp is managed by the system and should not be sent in the API request.

abuse_category.description: Category of abuse being reported, e.g., 'spam', 'offensive', 'harassment', 'illegal'. May be changed by admins during moderation triage. Enforced by business logic.

reason.description: Detailed moderation/admin explanation or justification, subject to business validation. May be edited to clarify or correct initial submission.

status.description: Current workflow status of the abuse report. Typical values: 'pending', 'in_review', 'closed', 'rejected'. Only administrators may change status. Enforced as an enum or via business logic at a higher layer.

id.description: UUID primary key identifying this moderation action event. This is a globally unique, immutable reference for each record in the discussion_board_moderation_actions table, used for regulatory traceability, audit presentation, and direct hypermedia linkage from endpoints and compliance logs.

admin_id.description: UUID of the admin who performed the moderation action. Maps directly to discussion_board_admins.id. Used for accountability, permission enforcement, and compliance reporting.

oneOf.description: UUID referencing the associated article (discussion_board_articles.id) if the moderation action concerns a specific article.

target_article_id.description: UUID referencing the associated article (discussion_board_articles.id) if this moderation action concerns a specific article. This field is mutually exclusive with target_comment_id: at least one must be set, but not both. Used for direct linkage and compliance cross-tracing.

oneOf.description: UUID referencing the associated comment (discussion_board_article_comments.id) if this moderation action relates to a comment.

target_comment_id.description: UUID referencing the associated comment (discussion_board_article_comments.id) if this moderation action relates to a comment. This field is mutually exclusive with target_article_id: at least one must be set, but not both.

oneOf.description: UUID referencing the abuse report (discussion_board_abuse_reports.id) if this moderation action is in response to a report.

abuse_report_id.description: UUID referencing the abuse report (discussion_board_abuse_reports.id) if this moderation action is in response to a user report; otherwise null. Links compliance investigation and closes audit workflow loop.

action_type.description: Type/category of moderation action performed by the administrator. Commonly expected business values include: 'edit', 'delete', 'hide', 'warn'. This field is required for categorization and audit trace. May be extended with business-specific values. See moderation workflow documentation.

action_reason.description: Detailed free-text justification, rationale, or policy reference for the moderation action. Must provide a business or compliance basis for the action, suitable for regulatory audit and future forensic review. Required for transparency and compliance enforcement.

affected_data_ref.description: Description or reference for the specific data/content affected by this action. Typically a summary string, content hash, or file/artifact reference. Used in compliance trace and for incident recovery.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when this moderation action record was created (UTC, e.g., '2025-03-10T12:15:00Z'). Used for ordering, history audit, and retention compliance.

updated_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp indicating the most recent update or annotation to this moderation action event (UTC, e.g., '2025-03-10T12:20:00Z'). Used for compliance and regulatory annotations.

IDiscussionBoardModerationAction.description:
Comprehensive moderation action event record for the discussion board platform. This entity represents an immutable, append-only log of any core moderation action (edit, delete, hide, warn, etc.) carried out by an administrator against a target article or comment. Moderation actions are designed for full compliance, regulatory oversight, and audit trail completeness: each action must clearly reference the responsible admin actor, the affected resource (article or comment), the specific action taken, the full business rationale, and all critical context (such as cross-linkage to any associated user abuse report—which closes the audit loop). These records enforce traceability for all privileged actions and support monitoring, crisis review, and compliance exports. All timestamp fields use ISO8601 UTC format for regulatory interoperability. Mutually exclusive article and comment linkage ensures clean mapping for per-object workflow queries, and integration with abuse reports and audit logs is explicitly supported at the schema level.

Prisma model reference: discussion_board_moderation_actions.

IDiscussionBoardModerationAction.IReques.description:
Schema for advanced query, filter, and pagination of moderation actions in the discussion_board_moderation_actions table. Enables administrators to search through historical moderation records with criteria such as admin identity, target article/comment, action type, date range, and free-text searches by action reason. Incorporates all indexable fields for efficient and flexible auditing, and produces paginated lists compliant with scalable compliance workflows.

Supports filtering on all main foreign keys, string fields, and date-time columns. Can be extended with business-specific filter logic (e.g. status, audit flags, complex multi-field search) if defined by requirements. Used as the request body in the moderation actions list/search endpoint.

admin_id.description: Filter moderation actions by the admin (administrator) who performed them. Maps to admin_id FK in schema. Optional; omit for full dataset.

target_article_id.description: Filter for moderation actions affecting a specific article (discussion_board_articles.id). Optional and mutually exclusive with target_comment_id if desired.

target_comment_id.description: Filter for moderation actions affecting a specific comment (discussion_board_article_comments.id). Optional and mutually exclusive with target_article_id if desired.

abuse_report_id.description: Optional filter for moderation actions related to a particular abuse report. Maps to abuse_report_id. May be used for cross-audit workflows.

action_type.description: Filter for actions by their type. Business layer enforces allowed values such as 'edit', 'delete', 'hide', 'warn'. Optional.

action_reason.description: Full text search filter for the justification/explanation of the moderation action, applied to the action_reason column. Optional.

created_from.description: Filter for moderation actions created on or after this UTC datetime. For date-range queries. Optional.

created_to.description: Filter for moderation actions created on or before this UTC datetime. For date-range queries. Optional.

oneOf.description: Field by which to sort the results. Allowed values are 'created_at', 'action_type', 'admin_id'.
Field by which to sort the results. Allowed values are 'created_at', 'action_type', 'admin_id'.
Field by which to sort the results. Allowed values are 'created_at', 'action_type', 'admin_id'.

sort_by.description: Field by which to sort the results. Allowed values are 'created_at', 'action_type', 'admin_id'.

oneOf.description: Order in which to sort results: ascending ('asc') or descending ('desc').
Order in which to sort results: ascending ('asc') or descending ('desc').

sort_order.description: Order in which to sort results: ascending ('asc') or descending ('desc').

page.description: Page number for paginated query results. Must be 1 or greater.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return per page. Limits enforced by business config; typical max is 100.

id.description: Unique identifier for the administrator. References the discussion_board_admins.id field in the database.

email.description: Administrator's unique email address for privileged login, escalation notices, and audit traceability. Corresponds to discussion_board_admins.email.

display_name.description: Administrator's display name for moderator tools, platform audit logs, and transparency. See discussion_board_admins.display_name.

oneOf.description: URL to the admin avatar/profile picture for identification in logs/UIs, or null if no avatar image is set.

avatar_url.description: Optional admin avatar/profile picture, for team identification in logs and UIs. Corresponds to discussion_board_admins.avatar_url. Can be null.

is_locked.description: Indicates locked, banned, or suspended admin account status. Used to prevent privileged access, for investigation or policy.

oneOf.description: Timestamp for soft deletion for GDPR, key rotation, or similar admin lifecycle events.

deleted_at.description: Timestamp (ISO8601) of soft deletion for GDPR or key/permission rotation purposes. If set, the account is soft deleted.

created_at.description: Administrator account creation timestamp.

updated_at.description: Last timestamp the admin profile was modified.

IDiscussionBoardAdmin.ISummary.description:
Summary information of a discussion board administrator account. Contains essential profile and status fields only, omits sensitive credentials. Used for displaying admin identity in moderation logs or admin listings. Derived from the discussion_board_admins table.

Includes:
- Unique id (UUID)
- Email address (unique)
- Display name
- Optional avatar URL
- Locked/soft-deleted status
- Timestamps for creation and update

Does NOT include password or sensitive data.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.ISummary.description: Summary DTO for discussion board article entity. Represents a lightweight view for list and embedding scenarios; contains primary identification and context for an article, without large text fields or strong composition arrays. This summary includes essential properties for list display, context, and quick reference. Designed for high-performance queries and optimized list rendering in the discussion board. See full article entity (IDiscussionBoardArticle) for composition fields. Derived from the discussion_board_articles Prisma schema.

id.description: Primary key of the article, uniquely identifies an article post. Maps to discussion_board_articles.id.

title.description: Article title. Required by business rule (1–100 characters). Obtained from discussion_board_articles.title.

author.description: The user who authored the article. Provides summary information of the author (display_name, avatar, etc). For detailed user data, see the user entity. Transformed from author_user_id.

created_at.description: Datetime when the article was created. Used for sort and display. Maps to discussion_board_articles.created_at.

IDiscussionBoardArticleComment.ISummary.description: Summary/minimal representation of a comment, suitable for paginated or batch retrieval in list views or admin moderation panels. This summary now includes primary keys plus audit metadata (edit/deletion) required for moderation and compliance workflows. It presents only the core details for navigation and batch analytics, but covers all business reporting and moderation scenarios. For full comment history, use the detailed entity.

id.description: Unique identifier for a single comment summary record. From discussion_board_article_comments.id.

discussion_board_article_id.description: Parent article's unique ID for linking and context. From discussion_board_article_id field.

author.description: Summary user info (id, display_name, avatar_url, is_locked) for this comment's author. Used for attribution and moderation reporting.

body.description: Text of the comment in entirety—not a truncated excerpt—ranging from 1 to 1000 characters as per business rules.

created_at.description: Comment's creation time for sort order/sorting and timeline context. From created_at column.

updated_at.description: Timestamp marking the most recent update to the comment. Required for edit audit trail and moderation flags. From updated_at column.

oneOf.description: Timestamp of soft deletion if the comment has been deleted; null if the comment is currently active.

deleted_at.description: Timestamp of soft deletion for moderation. Null if the comment is currently visible; matches discussion_board_article_comments.deleted_at field.

IDiscussionBoardAbuseReport.ISummary.description:
Summary DTO for a single user-submitted abuse report or inappropriate content report record. Intended for list and administrative display. Omits heavy relational data and downward compositions for efficiency.

Represents a record of a report by a user about an article or comment, including core status and context. All abusive content review and moderation flows reference this object for initial triage. Based on the discussion_board_abuse_reports table in the Prisma schema.

id.description: Unique identifier for the abuse report record. Primary key from the discussion_board_abuse_reports table.

reporter.description: Summary information of the user who submitted the report. Transforms reporter_user_id foreign key to object.

target_article_id.description: Unique identifier of the reported article (if report concerns an article); null if the report only involves a comment.

target_comment_id.description: Unique identifier of the reported comment (if report concerns a comment); null if the report only involves an article.

abuse_category.description: Category/type of alleged abuse (e.g., 'spam', 'harassment', 'illegal', or other business-defined workflow enums).

reason.description: Reporter-supplied explanation or reason for the abuse report, as free text.

status.description: Current state of the report workflow; expected values include 'pending', 'in_review', 'closed', or 'rejected'.

created_at.description: Timestamp when this report was submitted.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the report status or details were last updated.

target_article_id.description: The UUID of the discussion board article being moderated by this action, or null if the action relates only to a comment. References discussion_board_articles.id. Optional depending on the moderation target.

target_comment_id.description: The UUID of the discussion board article comment being moderated, or null if the moderation action applies only to an article. References discussion_board_article_comments.id. Optional depending on the moderation target.

abuse_report_id.description: If this moderation action is in response to a user-submitted abuse report, the UUID referencing the report (discussion_board_abuse_reports.id); otherwise, null.

action_type.description: The type of moderation action performed by the admin. Expected business-level values include 'edit', 'delete', 'hide', 'warn', etc. Enforced by business logic for workflow categorization.

action_reason.description: Full text providing detailed rationale, justification, or business policy reference for this moderation action. Required for audit compliance and transparency.

affected_data_ref.description: Reference or summary of the data impacted by this moderation action. May be a content hash, file pointer, or business-level summary for audit tracking.

IDiscussionBoardModerationAction.ICreate.description: Schema for creating a new moderation action on the discussion board platform. Used by administrators to log actions (edit, delete, hide, warn) targeting articles or comments in response to user actions or abuse reports. Includes references to the admin actor (from auth context), target article or comment (only one required), optional abuse report reference, the action type, detailed reason/justification, affected data summary, and all required information for proper audit logging. Based on discussion_board_moderation_actions table and business compliance rules.

action_reason.description: Updated rationale or justification text for the moderation action. Only this and other updatable audit notes are permitted for update per compliance policy. Immutable fields such as action_type and targets cannot change.

affected_data_ref.description: Updated reference/summary of the data impacted by this moderation action. Only updatable if allowed by compliance policy; represents additional information for traceability.

IDiscussionBoardModerationAction.IUpdate.description: Schema for updating an existing moderation action by administrators in the discussion board platform. Permits revision of audit notes or affected data references for regulatory annotation, but forbids modification of historical actor, action type, or target object. Based on the fields permitted to change in discussion_board_moderation_actions as governed by audit and compliance requirements.

IDiscussionBoardAuditLog.IRequest.description: Query parameters for searching, filtering, and paginating audit log records for moderation, compliance, and administrative operations within the discussion board. Supports filtering by event type, admin actor, date range, and affected resources. Enables full-text search on audit_details, and provides advanced controls for audit/compliance team workflows. Does not require x-autobe-prisma-schema as this is used for search, not direct table mapping.

page.description: Page index for paginated results (1-based). Used for selecting which subset of results to return from the audit log query. Required for clients implementing pagination controls.

limit.description: Maximum number of log entries to return per page. Should not exceed business-configured limit for performance and compliance.

search.description: Full-text search query for audit_details or other relevant fields. Can be left blank to disable text search.

admin_id.description: Optional filter to restrict results to logs performed by this administrator (references discussion_board_admins.id).

event_type.description: Optional filter for specific audit event types (e.g., 'moderation_performed', 'compliance_override', 'manual_restore').

target_article_id.description: Optional filter for audit logs concerning the specified article. References discussion_board_articles.id.

target_comment_id.description: Optional filter for audit logs concerning the specified comment. References discussion_board_article_comments.id.

from.description: Include only audit events created at or after this ISO 8601 timestamp. Enables filtering by minimum date/time.

to.description: Include only audit events created at or before this ISO 8601 timestamp. Enables filtering by maximum date/time.

oneOf.description: Controls result sorting field. Accepts 'created_at' (default) or 'event_type'.
Controls result sorting field. Accepts 'created_at' (default) or 'event_type'.

order_by.description: Controls result sorting field. Accepts 'created_at' (default) or 'event_type'.

oneOf.description: Sort direction. Accepts 'asc' (ascending) or 'desc' (descending); default is 'desc'.
Sort direction. Accepts 'asc' (ascending) or 'desc' (descending); default is 'desc'.

order_dir.description: Sort direction. Accepts 'asc' (ascending) or 'desc' (descending); default is 'desc'.

IDiscussionBoardAuditLog.description: Represents an immutable audit log record capturing all critical moderation and administrative actions within the discussion board service. Each log entry records the responsible administrator (actor), referenced article/comment, related moderation action, event type, human-readable audit details, and event timestamp. Supports strict compliance and forensic traceability by reflecting the schema and business logic described in the original discussion_board_audit_logs Prisma model.

id.description: Primary key for the audit log record. Universally unique identifier as defined by discussion_board_audit_logs.id.

actor_admin.description: Reference to the admin actor who performed or authorized the auditable event. Populated from discussion_board_admins.

oneOf.description: Targeted article if this audit log references an article event. Foreign key to discussion_board_articles.id or null when only a comment is targeted.

target_article_id.description: Targeted article if this audit log references an article event. Foreign key to discussion_board_articles.id or null when only a comment is targeted.

oneOf.description: Targeted comment if this audit log references a comment event. Foreign key to discussion_board_article_comments.id or null when only an article is targeted.

target_comment_id.description: Targeted comment if this audit log references a comment event. Foreign key to discussion_board_article_comments.id or null when only an article is targeted.

moderation_action_id.description: References the corresponding moderation action this audit event relates to, as recorded in discussion_board_moderation_actions.id.

event_type.description: Type of audit event: e.g. 'moderation_performed', 'compliance_override', 'manual_restore', etc. Determined by moderation/business process.

audit_details.description: Free-text justification, detail, and reasoning for the audit event. May include policy explanation or case references.

created_at.description: Timestamp of audit event creation, recorded as an ISO 8601 datetime string.

IDiscussionBoardUserSession.ISummary.description:
Summary DTO for a user's login session, representing the essential session context for audit logs, device listing, and session management views. Reflects only fields present in the discussion_board_user_sessions Prisma table and omits sensitive connection metadata where feasible.

Provides public session context—such as unique session id, ip address (for trusted device display or security audit), connection origins (href/referrer), creation timestamp, and expiration status—to authorized user or admin UIs. Used in the context of session listing for account security, reviewing device history, or highlighting active vs. expired sessions. Excludes all authentication secrets, tokens, or session-specific keys. Follows the "Summary" contract for compact, performant response objects.

id.description: Unique identifier for the session. Matches the id field in discussion_board_user_sessions; serves as the session key for login and audit trail reference.

discussion_board_user_id.description: References the owning user account (discussion_board_users.id). Only the session owner or authorized admin may access this session info. This field exists in the underlying database and is included in the summary DTO for audit, traceability, and cross-account listing in administrative interfaces.

ip.description: IP address from which the session was established. Used in security reviews and account activity listings. Matches the ip field in discussion_board_user_sessions.

href.description: Connection URL at session creation, representing where the login or session was initiated. Matches the href column in discussion_board_user_sessions.

referrer.description: Referrer URL for the page that originated the session creation. Useful for traceability in browser-based or external login workflows. Matches the referrer field in discussion_board_user_sessions.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp representing when the session was started. Matches created_at in discussion_board_user_sessions.

expired_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp indicating when the session expired, or null if session is still valid/current. Matches expired_at in discussion_board_user_sessions.

id.description: Session unique identifier. References discussion_board_admin_sessions.id.

discussion_board_admin_id.description: References the administrator owning this session (discussion_board_admins.id).

ip.description: Session's originating IP address for incident review and admin login traceability.

href.description: Connection URL/location where the admin session was initiated. Used for audit context and tracing suspicious activity.

referrer.description: Referrer URL or entry point for admin login/session creation, for context and compliance.

created_at.description: Timestamp of session creation.

oneOf.description: Session expiration timestamp if expired.

expired_at.description: Session expiration ISO8601 timestamp, or null if active/valid.

IDiscussionBoardAdminSession.ISummary.description:
Summary information for one administrator login session on the discussion board. Contains session metadata for audit logging and security analysis. Does not include sensitive access tokens. Derived from the discussion_board_admin_sessions Prisma model.

Includes:
- Unique session id (UUID)
- Owning admin reference (UUID)
- Connection metadata (IP, href, referrer)
- Session lifecycle timestamps

For context and compliance tracking only.

IDiscussionBoardArticleAttachment.ISumma.description:
Summary DTO for a discussion board article attachment. Represents lightweight file/image metadata attached to an article, primarily used for list displays, attachment references, and dashboard summary views. Does not include the actual file content. Designed to support fast, minimal attachment lookups in responses via IDiscussionBoardArticle summary/list operations.

- Maps to a subset of fields in discussion_board_article_attachments Prisma model.
- Used for referencing, displaying and filtering file/image metadata, not for full download flows.
- Properties clarify what files are, their roles, and their classification per business attachment rules.
- See IDiscussionBoardArticleAttachment entity for detailed attachment information.

id.description: Unique identifier (UUID) for this attachment. Matches id field in discussion_board_article_attachments. Used for direct referencing, download, or administrative actions.

filename.description: Original uploaded file name as provided by the user, including file extension (example: "document.pdf" or "photo.png"). Should be filtered/displayed according to business-allowed filetype rule: JPEG, PNG, GIF for images; PDF, DOCX, XLSX, TXT, ZIP for documents/archives.

kind.description: Attachment category, either 'image', 'document', or 'archive'. Directly affects listing display icon/preview logic. Business logic is responsible for mapping file extensions/MIME types to these values.

mimetype.description: MIME type of the uploaded file (example: "image/jpeg", "application/pdf"). Used for download, file-type safety, and allowed formats check by business rule.

IDiscussionBoardModerationAction.ISummar.description:
Summary representation of a moderation action performed by a platform administrator on the discussion board. Used for dashboard, history list, or compliance audit views to summarize key details about moderation events.

- Covers only essential audit fields: action id, administering actor's id, moderation type, key target references, operation reason summary, and audit timestamp.
- Derived from discussion_board_moderation_actions Prisma model.
- Soft deletion does not apply; all actions are persistent.
- action_reason field summarizes the rationale or justification for the action (per compliance/business process).
- Nullability (target_article_id/target_comment_id) follows moderation target rules: only one is set, or both null for global actions.
- action_type should enumerate types allowed by business logic (e.g., 'edit', 'delete', 'hide', 'warn') for traceability.

id.description: Unique identifier (UUID) for the moderation action event. Used for audit traceability, historical lookup, and dashboards. Matches id field in discussion_board_moderation_actions.

admin_id.description: Platform administrator UUID who performed this moderated action. Links to discussion_board_admins.id. Enables accountability for moderator/auditor workflow.

oneOf.description: UUID of the article affected by the moderation action; if present, the action concerns an article.

target_article_id.description: If present, the ID of the article affected by this moderation action. Null when the action targets only a comment or is global.

oneOf.description: UUID of the comment affected by the moderation action; if present, the action concerns a comment.

target_comment_id.description: If present, the ID of the comment affected by this moderation action. Null for article-only or global actions.

action_type.description: Type/category of moderation event (e.g., 'edit', 'delete', 'hide', 'warn'). Used for timeline, audit filtering, and compliance context. Must conform to allowed action types in business logic.

action_reason.description: Summary rationale or justification for the moderation action, as entered by the moderator for audit/compliance. Essential for transparency, history, and denormalized auditing.

created_at.description: Timestamp (ISO 8601) of when this moderation event occurred/was officially recorded. Used for audit trails, historical timelines, and dashboard metrics.

IDiscussionBoardAuditLog.ISummary.description:
Summary of an audit log record for compliance/audit review on the discussion board. Suitable for embedding in moderator dashboards, trace reports, or compliance checklists. Provides essential snapshot information without full event details or artifact relationships. Documents actor, referenced object, action, details summary, and timestamp. Immutable once recorded (append-only); not directly editable except via compliance process. Derived from the 'discussion_board_audit_logs' Prisma table. See model for detailed relationships and field descriptions. This summary exposes only the most critical context for timeline or quick lookup views.

Derived from: discussion_board_audit_logs Prisma table.

id.description: Unique primary key for the audit log entry. Sourced from 'discussion_board_audit_logs.id'. Required for reference and audit trail linking.

actor_admin_id.description: Administrator's user ID who performed or is being audited for this log entry. References 'discussion_board_admins.id'. Used for actor lookups.

target_article_id.description: If the audit event concerns a specific article, its ID appears here. 'discussion_board_articles.id'. Null if event targets a comment or other item.

target_comment_id.description: If the audit event concerns a specific comment, its ID appears here. 'discussion_board_article_comments.id'. Null if event targets an article or general event.

moderation_action_id.description: Required. The moderation action this audit log traces, from 'discussion_board_moderation_actions.id'. Used for audit/integrity/cross-reference.

audit_event_type.description: Type or category of audit event. Examples: 'moderation_performed', 'compliance_override', 'manual_restore'.

created_at.description: Timestamp of audit entry creation, for timeline ordering and compliance review.
